title: Cloud Tasks and Cloud Scheduler: queues and cron in the platform

videos.script: Pub/Sub says something happened. A task says do this, once, at a rate you choose. This lesson is about work that must not all happen at once. {{queues}} First, the queue. It owns three decisions: how fast, how persistently, and as whom. The shop's confirmation emails go through one. {{handler}} Then the handler, and the duplicate it must survive. curl plays the queue on your laptop, and the second delivery of the same task sends nothing. {{retries}} Then the retry settings, worked out in seconds by a dozen lines of Python. Four retries end two and a half minutes after the first attempt. {{scheduler}} Last, Cloud Scheduler. It is cron run by Google, priced per job and not per run. Scheduler decides when, and the queue decides how fast.
